machines.title: Conveyors
machines.summary: Belt, roller and chain conveyors that move materials and products.
hazards: Entanglement of clothing, hair or gloves
Crushing at transfer points and take-ups
nip_points: Head and tail pulleys: belt running onto a pulley
Idler and return rollers along the belt
Skirts and chutes where hands reach in

guarding.detail: Enclose nip points at drive, head, tail, take-up and snub rollers so hands cannot reach in
Along the full length where people can reach, reset manually
Doors and hatches stop the conveyor when opened
Guard rails and crossovers so nobody climbs on the belt

before_start: Check guards are fitted and secure
Walk the line: nothing on the belt, no people near
Test the emergency stop and pull cords
Warn nearby workers before starting
Check start alarms or horns work
daily_checks: Belt tracks centrally, no fraying or damage
Rollers turn freely, no noise from bearings
Housekeeping: no spillage under or around the conveyor
hidden_hazards: Clearing a jam with the belt still live or stored in the tension
Take-up weights and springs that hold energy
Sudden restart by automatic controls after a stoppage
Dust build-up that can ignite or cause slips
Tail pulley hidden behind equipment
never: Never clean, lubricate or clear jams on a running conveyor
Never reach into a nip point
Never ride on a conveyor
Never remove a guard without LOTO

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.21 (fencing of machinery) and s.22 (work on or near machinery in motion) (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN 620 (continuous handling equipment) and EN ISO 14120 commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z432 (safeguarding of machinery); provincial OHS regulations
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.212 and 1910.219; ANSI/ASME B20.1 (conveyors); 29 CFR 1926.555 for construction

machines.title: Power Presses
machines.summary: Mechanical and hydraulic presses that stamp, form or cut metal.
hazards: Hand or arm crushed in the die area
nip_points: The die closing area between the ram and the bolster
The feed zone where material enters

guarding.detail: Prevents hands entering the point of operation. Feed through small openings at a safe distance
Both hands must be on the controls for the whole dangerous movement. Never bypass or tie down
Stops the ram when a hand enters. Safety distance depends on stopping time (ISO 13855)
Use tongs or magnets to feed and remove parts so hands never enter the die
Checks stopping time and prevents repeat stroke

before_start: Confirm the correct die and set-up are approved
Check guards and light curtain are working
Test the two-hand control, the e-stop and the brake
Check the die is clamped and clear of loose items
Operator is trained and authorised
daily_checks: Guards and interlocks in place and not bypassed
No oil leaks or loose bolts
hidden_hazards: Repeat stroke caused by clutch failure
Die setter's hands in the die while the press is live
Bypassed or taped two-hand buttons
Ram can fall under gravity when stopped
Stored energy in hydraulic accumulators
never: Never reach into the die area during operation
Never tie down or bypass two-hand controls or sensors
Never work in the die area without LOTO and blocks in place
Never use a damaged or unapproved die
energy_sources: Stored energy in accumulators and springs

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.21 and s.22 and state rules for power presses (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN 692 (mechanical presses) and EN 693 (hydraulic presses) commonly specified (verify)
legal.canada: CSA Z142 (power press operation) and CSA Z432
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.217 (mechanical power presses); ANSI B11.1

typical: Guard missing at point of operation

machines.title: Lathes and Drilling Machines
machines.summary: Rotating cutting machines: lathes, drill presses, milling machines.
hazards: Entanglement in rotating chuck or workpiece
Chuck key thrown from the chuck
nip_points: Belts, pulleys and gears in the headstock

guarding.detail: Interlocked guard that stops the spindle when opened
Adjustable guard around the drill bit and spindle
Clear screen to deflect chips and coolant
Within easy reach of the operator
Interlocked or fixed covers at the headstock

before_start: Check all guards and the chip shield are in place
Check the workpiece or tool is clamped firmly
Remove the chuck key and any tools from the machine before starting
Roll sleeves up, tie hair back and remove rings, watches and gloves
Check the speed is correct for the job
daily_checks: Coolant and swarf cleared, floor dry
hidden_hazards: Long swarf that wraps and cuts
Hair or clothing caught by slow rotation
Hot chips and sharp edges
Loose workpiece thrown out
Coolant mist and slippery floors
never: Never wear gloves, loose sleeves, rings or dangling items near rotating parts
Never leave the chuck key in the chuck
Never measure or touch a rotating workpiece
Never use hands to remove swarf. Use a hook or brush with the machine stopped
Never clean or adjust while the machine is running
energy_sources: Mechanical (spindle inertia, gravity of the head)

legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN ISO 23125 (lathes) and EN 12717 (drilling) commonly specified (verify)
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.212 and 1910.219; ANSI B11.6 (lathes) and B11.8 (drilling, milling and boring)

typical: Operator wearing gloves or loose clothing

machines.title: Grinders and Abrasive Wheels
machines.summary: Bench and pedestal grinders and other abrasive wheel machines.
hazards: Wrong wheel for the machine speed
nip_points: Gap between the wheel and the tool rest
Exposed wheel area where fingers can be drawn in
Open side of the wheel near the guard

guarding.detail: Strong enough to contain pieces if the wheel bursts. Fitted and set correctly
Adjust to no more than 3 mm (1/8 in) from the wheel face (OSHA 1910.215)
Adjust to no more than 6 mm (1/4 in) from the wheel as it wears (OSHA 1910.215)
Fixed shield in front of the operator
Capture dust at the wheel

before_start: Check the wheel type and speed rating match the machine
Check the wheel for cracks. Tap test as trained
Let a new wheel run with the guard in place before use
Check tool rest and tongue guard are set
Wear eye and face protection
daily_checks: No cracks or chips in the wheel
Tool rest and tongue guard adjusted for the wheel wear
Wheel is not worn below its minimum size
hidden_hazards: Cracked wheels not obvious to the eye
Wheel speed higher than the rating
Work jammed between wheel and rest
Dust from metals that can ignite
Worn wheels that expose more of the arbor
never: Never use a wheel with a crack, chip or damage
Never remove or loosen the guard
Never grind on the side of a straight wheel
Never exceed the maximum speed marked on the wheel
Never use gloves that can be caught
energy_sources: Mechanical (wheel inertia, coasts after switch off)

legal.india: Factories Act 1948 s.21 and s.22; relevant IS code for abrasive wheels (verify)
legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN 13218 (stationary grinding machines) and EN 12413 (abrasive products) (verify)
legal.usa: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.215 (abrasive wheel machinery); ANSI B7.1

machines.title: Forklifts (Machine Safety View)
machines.summary: Powered industrial trucks: guards, stability and operator protection.
nip_points: Between truck and rack or wall
Articulation points on pivot steer axle

guarding.detail: Protects the operator from falling objects
Stops loads falling back onto the operator
Seat belt or restraint system worn always
Horn, lights, reversing alarm and blue spot light
Speed limit or limiter in pedestrian areas

before_start: Daily check: brakes, steering, horn, lights, tyres, forks, mast and chains
Check the load rating plate and the load is within capacity
Check the seat belt works and is worn
Operator is authorised and trained
Route clear and pedestrians separated
daily_checks: Forks free of cracks and wear
Chains and hoses not leaking or damaged
hidden_hazards: Rear-end swing during turns
Raised forks that cannot be seen
Battery charging hydrogen
Poor visibility with high loads
Uneven floors and ramps
never: Never carry passengers
Never raise people on forks without an approved platform
Never travel with a raised load
Never leave the truck with forks up or key in

legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN ISO 3691-1 (industrial trucks) commonly specified (verify)

machines.title: Air Compressors, Receivers and Boilers
machines.summary: Pressure equipment: air compressors, air receivers, steam and hot water boilers.
hazards: Fire and fuel gas explosion in boiler rooms

guarding.detail: Correctly set, tested and never blocked or plugged
Fixed guards on all drives

guarding.type: Pressure gauges and water level gauges
guarding.detail: Working and calibrated, readable

guarding.type: Low-water cut-off and flame failure devices
guarding.detail: Boiler controls that shut down safely
Drain air receivers regularly

before_start: Check the safety valve is free and not tampered with
Check pressure and water level gauges
Drain condensate from air receivers per the schedule
Check guards on belts and couplings
Check ventilation in the boiler or compressor room and CO detection if fuel fired
daily_checks: No leaks of air, steam, water or fuel
Certificates and statutory inspection in date
Room is clear, ventilated and free of oil and rags
hidden_hazards: Corrosion inside receivers that cannot be seen
Condensate and rust weakening the shell
Safety valves that stick shut
Unreleased pressure in lines and receivers
Combustion air blocked in boiler rooms
never: Never plug, adjust or tamper with a safety valve
Never exceed the rated pressure
Never open or work on pressure parts that are not isolated and depressurised
Never use an uncertified or overdue pressure vessel

legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; client and Civil Defence requirements; ASME and PED commonly specified (verify)

machines.title: Guillotine and Shearing Machines
machines.summary: Machines that cut sheet metal, paper or plastic with a blade.
hazards: Cuts from sharp blades and offcuts
nip_points: The blade and the hold-down area

guarding.detail: Prevents fingers reaching the blade. Distances per ISO 13857
Stops the blade when a hand enters
Prevents accidental stepping on the pedal
For machines that do not use light curtains
Stop access to the back gauge area when running

before_start: Check guards and light curtains are working
Test the e-stop
Check the blade is sharp and securely held
Check the foot pedal guard is in place
Clear the table of tools and loose items
hidden_hazards: Blade changing without blocks or lockout
Operator not aware of the second person at the back
Gravity fall of the blade when stopped
Offcuts that cut hands
Light curtain muting bypassed
never: Never put hands under the blade or hold-down
Never bypass light curtains or guards
Never change blades without LOTO and blocking
Never operate with two people unless controls are designed for it

legal.gulf: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 33 of 2020; EN 13985 (guillotine shears) commonly specified (verify)

machines.title: Industrial Mixers and Blenders
machines.summary: Ribbon, paddle, planetary and tank mixers in food, chemical and other plants.

guarding.detail: Stops agitator when the lid or guard is opened
Prevents hands reaching the agitator
Within reach at the operating position
Prevents opening while running
Treat mixer interiors as confined spaces

before_start: Check interlocks stop the agitator when opened
Check the grate and guards are fitted
Check the contents and cleaning chemicals are known
Confirm nobody is inside before closing the lid
Check ventilation and dust controls
hidden_hazards: A person inside during start-up
Residue or product that bridges and then collapses
Static discharge and dust ignition
Hot or cold product
Chemicals used in cleaning
never: Never reach into a mixer while the agitator can move
Never defeat interlocks
Never enter a mixer without LOTO, a permit and a standby
Never start without checking the inside is empty

legal.canada: CSA Z432 and provincial confined space regulations

loto.title: 7-Step Lockout/Tagout (LOTO)
loto.principle: Every person who works on the equipment puts on their own lock. If you did not lock it, you cannot trust it.

steps.title: Prepare
do: Read the machine-specific LOTO procedure
Identify every energy source: electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, mechanical, gravity, thermal, chemical
Identify all isolation points and who is affected
steps.verify: Can you list every energy source and its isolation point?
mistakes: Missing a second power source or a stored energy source
Using a general procedure instead of the machine one

steps.title: Notify
do: Tell operators, supervisors and nearby workers that the machine will be locked out
Agree the time and expected duration
steps.verify: Does everyone affected know and agree?

steps.title: Shut down
do: Stop the machine using the normal stop control
Wait for all movement to stop
Follow the correct shutdown order
mistakes: Using the emergency stop as the normal stop
Isolating a machine that is still running

steps.title: Isolate
do: Operate the isolating devices: switches, breakers, valves, disconnects
Isolate every energy source
Use physical isolation, not a control button or software
steps.verify: Is every isolating device in the safe position?
mistakes: Using a push-button stop as an isolator

steps.title: Lock and tag
do: Fit your personal lock to each isolation point
Attach a tag with your name, date and reason
Use group lock boxes for large jobs, each person with their own lock on the box
Keep your key with you
steps.verify: Does every isolation point have a lock and tag, and does each worker have a personal lock?
mistakes: Tag only without a lock where a lock is possible

steps.title: Release stored energy
do: Bleed pressure from hydraulic and pneumatic lines
Block or support raised parts and loads
Release springs and tensioned parts
Allow hot parts to cool, discharge capacitors
Purge chemical or steam lines
steps.verify: Has all stored and residual energy been released or blocked?

steps.title: Verify isolation
do: Try to start the machine using the normal controls. Return the controls to off
For electrical work use a tester: test the tester, test the circuit, test the tester again
Check gauges read zero and nothing can move
Only then start work
steps.verify: Did the machine fail to start and do tests show zero energy?
mistakes: Using a tester that has not been proved

restoration: Clear tools and materials from the machine
Check that everyone is clear of the machine
Remove each lock and tag by the person who put it on
Inform affected workers and then re-energise and test the machine
rules: Only the person who fitted a lock may remove it
If the owner is not available, follow the formal lock removal procedure with management authorisation and make every effort to contact the owner first
At shift change, hand over locks with a documented handover
Contractors use their own locks and are part of the procedure
LOTO is for servicing and maintenance, and for clearing jams and cleaning where guards are removed
Review the procedure at least once a year and audit it with a periodic inspection

energy_types.isolation: Lock the disconnect, test for dead
Close and lock valves, bleed pressure
Close and lock valves, vent the air
Wait for stop, block or release tension
Lower to the ground or block securely

energy_types.examples: Steam, hot water, hot surfaces, cold
energy_types.isolation: Isolate and allow temperature to return to safe level

nip_points.title: Nip-point and pinch-point checks

types.name: In-running nip
types.detail: Two rotating parts, or a belt and a roller, draw in hands or clothing
types.example: Belt running onto a conveyor pulley, rolls on a printing machine

types.name: Pinch point
types.detail: A moving part closes against a fixed part
types.example: Press ram and die, door closing on a frame

types.name: Shear point
types.detail: Two parts move past each other like scissors

types.name: Entanglement point
types.detail: A rotating shaft or part catches clothing, hair or gloves
types.example: Lathe chuck, drive shaft, drill bit

types.name: Crush point
types.detail: Part of the body trapped between moving and fixed objects
types.example: Forklift mast and overhead guard, gates

walk_steps: Stop and look at the machine with the power off first
Trace every moving part and ask: what could catch a finger, a sleeve or hair?
Check each nip and pinch point has a fixed guard, an interlocked guard or a safe distance
Test that a guard cannot be reached around, over, under or through (ISO 13857 safety distances)
Check the emergency stop is within reach and works
Check the guard cannot be left off or bypassed without detection
Report any exposed point and tag out the machine until fixed
tips: Guards must stay fitted and not be easy to defeat
Safe distance depends on the size of opening and the distance to the hazard (ISO 13857)
Loose clothing, long hair, rings and gloves near rotating parts must be controlled
